subject: I don't know what Shiny is doing - Server.R code interpreted differently than console code

messages.author: 13b673b6027a537c
messages.subject: I don't know what Shiny is doing - Server.R code interpreted differently than console code
parts:
Sorry.  This is probably the type of question that takes too much work to answer.

So I have set up a shiny app that is supposed to add html syntax formatting to Stata code and hopefully other coding languages.
http://spark.rstudio.com/fsmart/RStylizer/

It seems to be working ok at recognizing commands highlighting them.  However, when it comes to the lines of code dealing with recognizing comments it does not recognize the grep("[:*:]", txt)) command.  Even when it recognizes the "//" comment structure, it includes the first part of the comment.start html tags but does not close them.

Try inputing the following example into the Shiny application.
https://gist.github.com/EconometricsBySimulation/6235945

So, this seems so far like purely a programming error with regex in grep not being structured properly.  However, I have tested the formatting code by running the code just in R (lines 14-100, uncommenting line 14) on https://github.com/EconometricsBySimulation/RFormatter/blob/master/server.R#L14

And it seems to run correctly when I just run the code in the R console running version 3.0.1.  However, it produces different output when passed through the shiny's server.R script.

I think shiny was built on an older version of R (2.25?).  Could that be the source of the problem.

Sorry for such a lengthy question.  I hate asking other to debug my code but I am not sure why the same code should run differently on Shiny than it does on my console.

Thanks so much for any help you can provide,
Francis

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: I don't know what Shiny is doing - Server.R code interpreted differently than console code
parts:
I can't imagine that Shiny would be changing the behavior of grep(). Does it work when you run it locally on your machine, presumably with R 3.0.1?

If that doesn't work, I suggest inserting a browser() just before the grep() and then examine the txt variable and whether the grep works. (This has to be done locally, not on Spark.)

Shiny for your system should have been built with R 3.0.1. It would be helpful if you include the output of sessionInfo().

-Winston

messages.author: 13b673b6027a537c
messages.subject: Re: I don't know what Shiny is doing - Server.R code interpreted differently than console code
parts:
Ok, great!  I think I know what is going on.  My sample code relied upon the "readLines" command which inherently breaks different lines of code into different values of a vector or list.  However, the way shiny is handling it is as if each the entire block of code is one text block.  All I need to do is txt <- unlist(strsplit(txt, split="\n")).

Perfect!
Thanks man,
Francis
